text:
In the previous story, every person followed exactly the same strategy to solve the problem.

This type of problem-solving approach has a name.

It is called **recursion**.

title: What is recursion?
text:
Recursion is a way of solving a problem by solving a smaller problem of the same kind.

> In programming, recursion is implemented by allowing a function to call itself.

Like in the story, Raghav asks Tarun, Tarun asks Amrit, and so on.
codeNote: This code is an example of recursion, since get_row_number() is calling itself.

title: Base Case
text:
Can you recall when the chain of asking questions stopped? It stopped when the question reached the last person.

This is what is known as the **base case**.

**Base Case:** the condition at which the function will not call itself, and will return a value instead.

Like in the story, the first person was the base case. When the question reached him, he did not ask anyone — he replied "Row 1".
codeNote: When the condition is_anyone_sitting_infront_of_me becomes False, that is the base case, and the function returns 1.

title: Recursive Case
text:
Why did this chain of asking questions eventually stop? It stopped because every time a person asked the question, it moved closer to the person sitting in the first row (the base case).

This is what is known as the **recursive case**.

**Recursive Case:** the part where the same problem is solved again, but in a smaller form that moves closer to the base case.

question: Can every problem be solved using recursion?
answer:
No. Recursion is useful when:

- the problem can be divided into a smaller problem of the same kind
- there is a clear stopping point
